newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares fall, foreign firms seek phosphates.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares fall, foreign firms seek phosphates.

text.p: Shares on the Amman exchange fell 0.11 percent on Wednesday at the end of weekly trade in high turnover boosted by foreign interest, brokers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index slipped 0.17 points to 153.37 points in business worth 2.46 million dinars ($3.47 million).
"There was a slight decline, but in general the market is stable," said analyst Mohammed Abdallah of Pearl Consulting.
A shallow 0.50 dinar fall to 253 dinars in heavily-traded Arab Bank led the official market index down.
But brokers reported strong interest for the second day running in Jordan Phosphate Mines, which rose 0.10 dinars to 3.40 in trade worth 249,000 dinars.

"This company is expected to make net profit this year of up to 20 million dinars ($28 million)," Abdallah said of the company. He said its six-month pre-tax profit to June this year stood at 13 million dinars.
"It's very attractive at this price and it seems that many institutions, mainly foreign, are interested in it," Abdallah said.
Jordan International Trading Centre rose 0.03 dinars to 0.71 dinars, but brokers said it was in relatively light trade prompted by end-of-year portfolio shuffling.
Overall 32 shares fell on Wednesday. Fifteen rose and six traded but closed unchanged.
